hints: Integrate $f'(x) = kx^2 - 2x$ to get $f(x) = \frac{1}{3}kx^3 - x^2 + c$.
walkthrough:
Integrate the derivative with respect to $x$:
$$f(x) = \int (kx^2 - 2x) dx = \frac{1}{3}kx^3 - x^2 + c$$

Substitute the known point $(0, 2)$ into the curve equation to find $c$:
$$2 = \frac{1}{3}k(0)^3 - 0^2 + c \implies c = 2$$

Substitute the second known point $(3, -1)$ into $f(x) = \frac{1}{3}kx^3 - x^2 + 2$:
$$-1 = \frac{1}{3}k(3^3) - 3^2 + 2 = 9k - 9 + 2 = 9k - 7$$

ai_rubric.Finding a Curve from Its Derivatives: Integrates to $\frac{1}{3}kx^3 - x^2 + c$ (M1, A1). Substitutes $(0, 2)$ to find $c = 2$ (DM1). Substitutes $(3, -1)$ (DM1) to obtain $k = \frac{2}{3}$ (A1).
